$comment: Shared test vectors for the quote matcher (issue #20, t5). The Python matcher (associate/accuracy/matcher.py) and the TypeScript matcher (.pi/extensions/associate/lib/matcher.ts) must return the same verdict, reason and nearest span on every case. Both test suites read this one file.
normalisation: Each line of the saved text and of the quote loses a leading '<digits><tab>' read line stamp; then every run of space, tab, newline, carriage return, form feed and vertical tab becomes one space and the ends are trimmed. Case and punctuation are never changed. Lengths and offsets count Unicode code points.
nearest_span: Only on a refusal for a quote absent from the saved text. Let q be the normalised quote and t the normalised saved text. matched is the largest k such that the first k code points of q occur in t (0 when none does). offset is the lowest position in t where that k-prefix occurs (0 when matched is 0). text is the window of t that starts at offset and is as long as q, clipped at the end of t.

literal_comment: A fact value is a literal, and must occur inside its quote, when it is a string with no whitespace (trimmed), a JSON number or a JSON boolean. A number is written as ECMAScript Number::toString writes it (String(n) in TypeScript, which is what JSON.stringify gives): the shortest decimal that reads back as the same double, with no '.0' on an integer-valued number (7.0 is '7'), '0' for -0, plain digits from 1e-6 up to below 1e21 and exponent form outside that ('1e-7', '1e+21'); an integer beyond 2^53 is first rounded to the nearest double, as JSON.parse does. A boolean is 'true' or 'false'. Null, objects, arrays and non-finite numbers are not literals. Both checkers must give each value below the same literal (null: not a literal).
contract_comment: A min_quote_length that is not a positive integer (missing, null, zero, negative, a fraction, a string, a boolean, an array or object) is a broken contract. The checker fails closed: every fact is refused with reason quote_short before its source is looked up, and its flag detail names the contract value. An integer-valued number such as 8.0 is a positive integer. Each case runs contract_input with the accuracy contract's min_quote_length replaced by the case's value (removed when the case has none) and compares accepted, per-fact id/verdict/reason/check, per-verdict id/outcome/reason/check and the report's flags.
